tag: Episode 45 · The Moon and the Sun
title: The Moon and the Sun

beats.t: Card Eighteen, the Moon. Two moons hung in the sky. One shone coldly. The other was black as its shadow.
A tower stood on either side of the path. Far away, a dog and wolf cried in turn. There was no way to tell which was the dog.
The Moon has one rule. Don't trust what you see.
Then what do we trust? Walk with our eyes shut?
Trust each other. Hold hands, call names, and check that someone answers.
Yeoni touched the notebook in their pocket. Its paper corner brushed their fingertips. That alone was a little reassuring.
(I don't know the face of the person on my side. But I know the handwriting. That's enough.)
Every puddle reflected a moon. Every puddle reflected Yeoni. Even when Yeoni stopped, the Yeoni in the water stopped half a beat late.
That's been copying me. But a little late each time.
Don't look. Step over the puddles, not in them.
Then mist descended. Ankles to knees, knees to shoulders. In an instant.
Hey, hands! Hold hands!
Yeoni reached out. Something brushed their fingertips, then slipped away. Everyone's voices receded into the mist.
Seo Hanbi stood with the umbrella open. Its taped ribs pushed back a little mist. Only Yundal remained beside her.
Moka and Yeoni went the other way. From the sound of it.
Didn't you say this was a card where we can't trust sounds?
True. So believe only half of what I'm saying too.
Footsteps approached through the mist. First a yellow bag appeared. Then Yeoni's face.
Hanbi! Found you. Yundal too.
Seo Hanbi began stepping forward, then stopped. Yeoni's sneakers were dry. After all those puddles.
Where's Moka?
We got separated over there. More importantly, Hanbi. I've been thinking.
Wasn't it your fault Neo got eaten?
The mist went quiet. Neither dog nor wolf cried.
Yeoni.
It was you in the first spring too. You opened the door. This time, you stood in front, and Neo got eaten.
Yeoni, that's...
Stay out of this, Yundal. This is between us.
Seo Hanbi's umbrella tip trembled. Her lips moved to answer, but no sound emerged. Those were the words she wrote in her ledger every night.
Yes. That's why I'm trying to repay...
Then give me the umbrella first. It was mine to begin with.
Rain began falling through the moonlight. Then more footsteps ran through the mist. Splash, splash. Straight through the puddles.
A second Yeoni appeared, soaked from head to sneakers. Their knees bore signs of a fall. Moka followed, panting.
What is that?! Why are there two Yeonis?!
Ah. Can't even half believe this.
Wet Yeoni looked at dry Yeoni. Dry Yeoni looked back. Their faces were identical, down to the swelling beneath their eyes.
What are you? What are you doing with my face?
I was about to ask you. Hanbi, that's the fake. Remember the thing smiling in the puddle?
Seo Hanbi looked between them. Dry Yeoni's smile was familiar. So familiar she couldn't breathe.
Let's verify. Yeoni's birth date and time.
July 6, 2002. Eight thirty. Eulhae Day Pillar.
Right. That's me. But that thing knows too!
Both correct. Black Moon eats Four Pillars charts. Numbers won't distinguish them.
Then my turn. Yeoni, how many stars did you first give me?
Two. Because the flavor was a crime.
Two! Seriously, it knows that too?
Both right again. This is driving me crazy.
The rain thickened. Wet Yeoni's teeth chattered. Dry Yeoni stood in the rain without getting wet. No one was calm enough to point it out.
The same face either way, rainwater. You couldn't choose in the first spring either.
Seo Hanbi raised her head. That voice. The one from behind the bus-stop bench, the one that first gave her the ledger.
I couldn't then. I can now.
Seo Hanbi closed the umbrella. Rain poured directly onto her head. Cold water soaked into her coat.
Dry Yeoni reached toward the umbrella in her hand.
Good. Give it here. It's mine.
Wet Yeoni moved too. Teeth chattering, staggering toward Seo Hanbi. Then they raised their bag to cover her head, leaving their own in the rain.
Idiot, why close the umbrella? You'll catch a cold.
Rain parted around the yellow bag. A small roof formed above Seo Hanbi. Clumsy, crooked, only half a roof.
The real Yeoni offers an umbrella first. Never asks to take one.
And if there's no umbrella, even a bag.
Seo Hanbi turned toward dry Yeoni. The folded umbrella's tip aimed at its chest.
Take off that face. It's not a face you get to own.
Dry Yeoni's smiling face cracked. Black light seeped through. The corners of its mouth split to its ears.
A pity. I meant to use it for longer this time.
The face fell away in pieces. Beneath it was nothing. One black circle devoured moonlight: the dark one of the two moons.
But it doesn't matter. Inside the Moon card, I can become anything. Your mother, your friends, even that cat.
Faces appeared in the mist: Yeoni, Seo Hanbi, Moka. Behind them stood someone with silver hair and dark blue clothes.
Neo.
The name escaped first. Yeoni couldn't recall who he was, but at the sight of the silver coat hem, their fingertips trembled.
Yeoni, that's a fake. The real one's clothes weren't that intact. His cuffs were frayed from hiding his injured arm.
Why tell me that now? It makes me want to see him more.
Enough. Everyone move. Fire for lies.
Moka struck his matches. Both remaining matches at once. Flame swelled between his fingers, then surged into the sky.
The sun rose. Card Nineteen, the Sun. Mist burned away in an instant. Faces hidden in moonlight curled like paper and vanished.
When they opened their eyes, they stood on a familiar stage beneath a noon sun. The world inside the Sun card resembled Moka's island.
Our island. The stage from the day the sun returned.
Moka, you really were the sun. Raising it with two matches.
Meaning I've used both. I'm empty-handed now. You're responsible.
Shall I put it in the ledger? Two matches, outstanding.
You said that ledger won't write anymore!
Instead of answering, Seo Hanbi shook out her wet hair and offered Yeoni a hand. Yeoni took it. Both were still drenched.
Hanbi. Thank you for what you said. But even I got confused. I thought that thing might be me.
I was confused too. The smiling faces were identical.
Then how did you choose?
The wet one. You're always the wet one, Yeoni.
A door stood open behind the Sun card's stage. A trumpet sounded beyond it. Card Twenty, Judgement.
Each time the angel in the sky blew its trumpet, a name rose from the ground. Names Black Moon had eaten. But they sank again. No one was there to call them.
Judgement calls. Someone has to call a name for it to rise.
Then I'll call them.
You have to know the owner. You only know a few names, Yeoni. I don't even know my own.
Yundal clenched his gloved hand. Black showed through the palm. The Void had grown a little.
Your hand. It's bigger than before.
I swallowed some mist today. I'm fine. It still fits in the glove.
The next door was Twenty-One, the World. A figure danced within a round laurel wreath. The card where the Fool's journey ended.
If that's the end, do we go to Black Moon now?
Normally it ends at Twenty-One. With the Fool as Zero, that's twenty-two cards. But look.
Beneath the laurel wreath, a narrow gap stood between the cards. Wide enough for one more card. Wind leaked through it.
[ 23 · THE DOOR ]
Letters appeared above the gap, then vanished. Yeoni had seen them before. In their room on the first night, before all this began.
That door. I know that door. It was in my room.
The gap widened, revealing a wooden door. Its handle was worn; the place for a nameplate was blank. No name at all.
An empty nameplate this time. Nothing to read.
That's scarier, kid.
Yundal stood before the door and removed his glove. The black circle in his palm tilted toward it, like water flowing downhill.
Beyond this, it smells like my palm. The smell of emptiness.
The Void. Black Moon's home. And probably where Mr. Cat is.
Then open it.
Very decisive. Once we enter, all five skies collapse into it. Are you ready?
I wrote it in my note. Going, even without remembering.
Yeoni gripped the handle. Cold. Then came a sound from the other side. Very faint, but unmistakable.
“Your socks. Wear matching ones.”
Yeoni's hand froze on the handle. They didn't know whose voice it was. But the tears came first. They looked down at their feet. Mismatched socks.
